title: Transporting a Panhard Dyna Z12 after purchase: trailer, loading and restraint
author: codex-blog-rewrite
excerpt: Dimensions, weight, access, seized wheels, winch, restraint points and loose parts: bring a Z12 home without turning collection into a road test.
content:
The seller says the Dyna Z12 starts and suggests “trying the drive home”. After a long lay-up, that merely transfers risk to the first miles: old tyres, unknown brakes, a weakened hose or incomplete cooling. A trailer costs less than a breakdown on a fast road and allows the project to begin in the workshop rather than on the hard shoulder.

Select the trailer before the sale

Club Panhard tables give Z12 a length of 4.58 m, width of 1.668 m and weight of about 875 kg. These figures start selection but do not replace usable carrier dimensions: bed and track width, space between mudguards, payload, ramp length and winch capacity. A car loaded with parts or non-standard equipment may weigh more.

Tow vehicle, trailer, coupling and driver’s licence must match current authorised masses. Relevant values appear on registration documents and plates. French Service-Public maintains licence categories, while the Highway Code requires precautions that prevent a load causing danger or damage. A specialist vehicle carrier is simpler than an improvised legal interpretation on collection day.

Obtain five facts about the site

  1. Access: gate width, height, slope, soft ground, turn and room to align.
  2. Wheels: does each rotate, is a tyre flat, is a rim seized?
  3. Steering: do front wheels follow the wheel and is the key available?
  4. Brakes: does the handbrake release and is the pedal mechanism free?
  5. Parts: volume, weight and number of boxes, panels, seats or extra engines.

A photograph from the road towards the car often explains access better than words. If the trailer cannot approach, winch cable length, slope and guiding arrangements change. A completely seized wheel may need dollies or a properly equipped professional.

Do not use the engine as a winch

Starting the car solely to climb the ramps combines uncertainties: temporary fuel, stuck clutch, uneven brakes and a driver in a narrow space. Even a car capable of movement is more safely winched with the engine stopped, one person steering and another watching alignment.

Ramps need adequate capacity and an angle that clears the underside. A loose board can slip. Before pulling, confirm neutral, released handbrake, functioning steering and clearance for low components.

Fragile points on an old car

Polished aluminium bumpers and overriders are not towing points. Nor are steering links, pipes, floor panels or corroded areas. A hook attached to the first convenient component can distort a scarce part before the car reaches the bed.

Z12 structure is organised around floor, sills and crossmembers. Where condition is unknown, the carrier needs warning before choosing a pulling or support point. Suitable wheel straps normally restrain through the tyres and avoid compressing suspension with body straps. The exact system still follows carrier-manufacturer instructions.

Position the car through load data

Longitudinal position determines coupling load and trailer behaviour. Too far rearwards can create instability; too far forwards can overload the tow vehicle’s rear axle or coupling. “Engine first” is not a measurement. Use the carrier’s specified distribution and stay within every permitted mass.

Z12 is front-wheel drive with engine and gearbox ahead. This affects balance, but parts stored in boot or cabin alter it. Heavy objects are better carried separately and restrained in a vehicle intended for them.

Restrain four wheels and secure openings

All four wheels are secured using the trailer system, sound straps, correct angles and no contact with sharp edges. Gear and parking-brake position follow carrier guidance and known mechanical condition. Tension receives a second check after loading.

Bonnet, boot and doors must latch mechanically. Dyna Z front doors open rearwards; a worn catch facing the airflow deserves supplementary security that does not harm paint or seals. A loose cover on an open trailer can flap and abrade the body, so protection needs to be designed and properly tensioned.

Loose parts travel as an inventory

Keys, plates, lamps, mouldings, hubcaps and documents do not remain loose in the cabin. Every box gets a number and photograph. Heavy items are blocked, small rare pieces stay with the buyer and leaking containers are emptied or contained.

The list accompanies the sale or transport order. At delivery it confirms that no seat, cooling panel or box remains with the seller. It also protects the cabin because a free metal component becomes a projectile under braking.

Check the combination during the journey

After the first miles, stop safely to inspect strap tension, car position, trailer wheels and rubbing. Repeat at breaks and after rough roads. Tow-vehicle and trailer tyre pressures, lighting and coupling were checked before departure.

Speed and following distance reflect the loaded combination and conditions. Secure restraint does not remove extra inertia or wind sensitivity. If a strap loosens or the trailer behaves unusually, stop before attempting any correction.

Prepare unloading as well

The destination is accessible, level and lit. The final space is ready before straps are removed: sound surface, chocks, room for winching or pushing and access around doors. One person never tries to hold a car without effective brakes on a ramp.

Once unloaded, photograph car and parts before storage. Note any damage, levels and leaks. Keep the battery disconnected and do not extend transport into a road test; recommissioning starts as a separate process.

Brief for the carrier

  • Panhard Dyna Z12, about 4.58 × 1.668 m and 875 kg excluding parts;
  • condition of every wheel, steering and handbrake;
  • corrosion or areas prohibited for pulling and support;
  • addresses, access, slope and contacts at both ends;
  • inventory and size of loose parts;
  • photographs before loading and at delivery.

This note prevents discovery of a seized wheel or narrow gate when the truck arrives. Transport becomes the first controlled operation of the project, not its first emergency repair.

Include the agreed collection window and a telephone contact who can make decisions on site. Waiting time, failed access and extra handling are easier to avoid when responsibilities are explicit before departure.
